verdict.rationale: Whether an engine can be consumed as an importable, bundleable, tree-shakeable dependency is a fair question for game engines targeting the web, so the axis applies. Nothing in the evidence shows Unity doing this. Its Package Manager and UPM registry deliver packages into the Unity Editor itself, and WebGL is a build-and-export target, not a library a web developer imports and bundles. Both are adjacent features, not this capability.

support.subject: As a web developer, the engine installs from a package registry into my existing toolchain — a library I import, bundle, and tree-shake like any dependency
